task.title: Set up a tasks-only folder with one command
task.description:
Workbook assumes it runs inside a clone of the project's code. A server that only shows and edits tasks has no use for the code, and should not have to hold a copy of it. This story makes a folder that holds a project's Workbook refs and nothing else a supported, one-command setup.

It mostly works already. On 0.6.0, in an empty folder set up by hand (`git init`, add the remote, set `user.email`, then `workbook setup --no-docs --no-skill`), setup pulled every task, and `list`, `create` with publication, and `serve` all worked. The refs for this project came to about 3 MB. That check ran against a remote holding only Workbook refs. A remote that also holds code is the case that matters and has not been tried.

## What is left to do

- **One command instead of four.** A person gives a remote URL in an empty folder and gets a working Workbook folder, with no Git knowledge needed.
- **Never download the code.** The hand-built folder keeps Git's default setting, which fetches every branch on a plain `git fetch`. The command sets the folder up so that neither Workbook nor a stray Git command pulls anything but Workbook refs.
- **Skip what has no meaning here.** Agent documentation and the skill are written for people working in the code, so this setup leaves them out.
- **Keep it working.** Nothing tests this shape today, so a later change could break it without anyone noticing.
- **Say what cannot work without the code.** Anything Workbook derives from code history, now or later, reports that it is unavailable in a tasks-only folder instead of showing a wrong answer.

## Decisions to settle before building

Settle these first and record the outcome on this task; each one that turns into real work becomes its own task depending on this one.

1. The command's name and shape: a mode of `workbook setup`, or its own command.
2. Whether the folder is an ordinary Git folder with no files checked out, as in the manual check, or a bare one. Setup writes `.workbook/` into the folder today.
3. Whether a tasks-only folder is recorded as such, so later commands can tell and refuse or adapt.

## Done when

- In an empty folder, one documented command given a remote URL produces a folder where `list`, `show`, `create`, `update` and `serve` work and changes publish.
- Against a remote that holds code as well as tasks, the folder ends up with no branches and none of the code, and a test proves it.
- Running the command again in a folder it already set up changes nothing and reports success.
- The automated suite covers this setup against temporary local remotes, both with and without code in them.
- The README and `docs/reference.md` describe the command and list what is unavailable without the code.
